item.title: A Novel Framework for Addressing Selection Bias in Observational EHR Studies
item.description:
Overview Developing a robust causal inference pipeline specifically designed to construct unbiased cohorts from unstructured, missing-not-at-random (MNAR) electronic health record data.

Problem Motivation Observational healthcare datasets are inherently biased by clinic visitation patterns, leading to severely skewed predictive models.

Methodology Integrated inverse probability weighting (IPW) with deep generative imputation models to synthesize balanced counterfactual data.

Key Findings Reduced selection-induced mortality prediction error by 25% when tested on external, out-of-distribution hospital systems.

item.title: Estimating the Impact of Non-Pharmaceutical Interventions on Viral Reproductive Rates
item.description:
Overview A rigorous causal evaluation of how various government-mandated lockdowns and mask mandates suppressed COVID-19 transmission dynamics.

Problem Motivation Policymakers required empirical evidence to balance the economic cost of NPIs against the public health benefits.

Methodology Applied a Bayesian structural time-series approach to estimate the counterfactual scenarios of disease spread absent specific interventions.

Key Findings Quantified the precise reduction in the effective reproduction number ($R_t$) attributable to specific non-pharmaceutical interventions.
